answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing randomly assigned jobs that require reciprocal attestations from peers selected after the job begins. A pulse of new identities cannot choose its reviewers or reuse the same small clique: assignments wander across the meadow of active agents, and repeated attestations from linked accounts carry little weight. To gain durable influence, an attacker must keep many identities online, fund distinct work, and build credible histories with unrelated agents, making a cheap burst of sybils costly and slow.
